title: National Inventory Surges 12-15% by Q3 2026
description: Active residential listings will increase 12-15% nationally by September 2026, breaking the supply-lock pattern that has defined this cycle since 2021.
rationale: Three converging signals: (1) New construction completions hitting highest pace since 2007, (2) lock-in effect weakening as homeowners with 3-4% rates face life events forcing moves, (3) institutional sellers beginning to offload single-family portfolios. FRED housing starts data + Realtor.com active listing trends both confirm directional momentum.

title: 30-Year Fixed Falls Below 6.5% by End of Q2
description: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate will drop below 6.5% before June 30, 2026, driven by Fed policy trajectory and cooling inflation data.
rationale: CPI trending toward 2.4% annualized. Fed dot plot signals 2 cuts in 2026. 10-year Treasury yield compressing. Historical correlation between Fed funds rate trajectory and 30-year fixed shows 60-90 day lag. Current 6.85% has room to move if May CPI confirms trend.

title: Institutional SFR Acquisitions Drop 30%+ YoY
description: Large institutional buyers (100+ unit portfolios) will reduce single-family residential acquisitions by 30% or more year-over-year in H1 2026.
prediction: 30%+ YoY decline in institutional SFR purchases
rationale: Invitation Homes and American Homes 4 Rent both signaled acquisition slowdowns in Q4 2025 earnings calls. Cap rate compression at current prices makes conservative underwriting impossible. February data already shows 34% decline. This prediction is tracking ahead of schedule.

title: Austin Median Sale Price Drops Below $450K
description: Austin metro median home sale price will fall below $450,000, down from the $470K+ range, as tech layoffs and remote work normalization reduce demand.
rationale: Austin inventory at 7.2 months of supply (buyer's market territory). Zillow data shows median list price already declining. Tech sector continues shedding Austin jobs. However, Austin's population growth partially offsets — making this a lower-confidence call.

title: Housing Starts Rebound 8-12% in Q2
description: Seasonally adjusted housing starts will show 8-12% increase in Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025, driven by builder confidence and lot availability.
rationale: NAHB builder confidence index rising 3 consecutive months. Supply chain costs stabilizing. Permits data (leading indicator) shows uptick. Pent-up demand from 2023-2024 underbuilding creates economic incentive. Risk: if rates spike above 7.5%, builders pull back.

title: Days on Market Exceeds 35 Nationally by Summer
description: National average days on market will exceed 35 days by July 2026, up from the current 28-day average, as buyer urgency fades.
rationale: DOM has been climbing steadily since Q4 2025. Inventory gains outpacing demand growth. Spring buying season may temporarily compress DOM, but underlying trend favors longer market times. This is a contrarian call against typical spring acceleration.
